questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a consumer market?

options.text: A market where goods are sold to individuals for personal use.
A market where businesses purchase goods for resale.
A market focused on non-profit organizations.
A market that includes government purchases.

questions.explanation: A consumer market is defined as one where individuals buy goods for their own use, distinguishing it from industrial markets which cater to businesses.

distractorRationale.b: This option describes industrial markets, not consumer markets.
distractorRationale.c: Non-profit organizations fall under organizational markets, not consumer markets.
distractorRationale.d: Government purchases are categorized under organizational markets.

options.text: The process of dividing a market into distinct groups.
The method of increasing product prices.
The strategy of selling to all consumers equally.

questions.explanation: Market segmentation is the process of dividing a market into distinct groups based on shared characteristics, which helps in targeting specific consumer needs.

distractorRationale.b: Increasing product prices is not related to market segmentation.
distractorRationale.c: Selling to all consumers equally ignores the benefits of targeted marketing.
distractorRationale.d: Competitor pricing analysis is a separate marketing strategy, not segmentation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a basis for market segmentation?
questions.explanation: Profit margins are related to financial performance, not a basis for segmenting a market. The other options are valid segmentation bases.

distractorRationale.a: Geography is a common basis for segmenting markets.
distractorRationale.b: Demography is a widely used segmentation criterion.
distractorRationale.c: Psychography focuses on consumer lifestyles and values, which is a valid segmentation basis.
